To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the histidyl residues in thyrotropin releasing hormone (TRH), which are essential for the biological activity of the peptide, are also essential for the peptide's binding affinity to TRH receptors and to the enzyme that degrades TRH.
TRH receptors and TRH-degrading enzyme have distinct binding properties for the TRH histidyl residue.

TRH binding to central TRH receptors is highly sensitive to replacement of the histidinyl residue of TRH, and that TRH binding at low affinity, high capacity sites in rat brain is mediated by TRH-degrading enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the structure of thyrotropine-releasing hormone receptors and the elucidation of their function.
the elucidation of the molecular basis of peptide hormone action.
the development and application of novel peptide libraries, and their application to the characterisation of peptide binding sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TRH receptors are high-affinity sites, while TRH-degrading enzyme is a low-affinity site.
the histidyl moiety of TRH is critical to the binding of TRH at its receptors in the rat brain cortex.
[3H][Me3His(2)]-TRH labels the TRH receptor, and [3H]-TRH labels a TRH-degrading enzyme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
[3H]THRH labels a single population of TRH receptors in rat brain, and that the binding affinity of a peptide at these receptors is determined by the amino acid at position 2.
the histidyl side chain is a major determinant of the binding of TRH and its analogues to TRH receptors, but not to TRH-degrading enzyme.
